prop:light-nuclei-a2-bond-tail:
Proposition The A = 2 \gamma\gamma bond on the four-strand tail, for every Markov parameter. Let K be a field with 2 \neq 0, and let z, h \in K. Write \mathrm{tr} for the Markov trace on H_4 with parameter z and h = q - q^{-1}, and use the letters S_i = \sigma_i, I_i = \sigma_i - h = \sigma_i^{-1} and A_i = \sigma_i - h/2. Let

V^3_k = (S_k I_{k+1})^3, \qquad
p = V^3_1\, S_1 A_1 A_2 S_1 S_1, \qquad
n = V^3_1\, A_1 A_1 I_2 S_1 S_1 .

Then

4\,\mathrm{tr}(p) = -\bigl(-h^{10}z + h^9z^2 - h^9 - 5h^8z + 5h^7z^2 - 5h^7 - 9h^6z + 9h^5z^2 - 9h^5 - 5h^4z + 4h^3z^2 - 5h^3 + h^2z - 6hz^2 + 2h - 4z\bigr),
4\,\mathrm{tr}(n) = -(h^2+4)\bigl(-h^8z + h^7z^2 - h^7 - 3h^6z + 3h^5z^2 - 3h^5 - 2h^4z + 2h^3z^2 - 2h^3 + h^2z - hz^2 + h - z\bigr),
4\bigl(\mathrm{tr}(p\,V^3_0) - \mathrm{tr}(p)\bigr) = h^4 (z^2 - hz - 1)(-h^7 + h^6z - 4h^5 + 3h^4z - 6h^3 + 2h^2z - 3h - 2z),
4\bigl(\mathrm{tr}(n\,V^3_0) - \mathrm{tr}(n)\bigr) = h^5 (h^2+1)(h^2+4)(hz - h^2 - 1)(z^2 - hz - 1).

In particular both bond terms vanish when z^2 - hz - 1 = 0, that is at z = q and z = -q^{-1}.

Setting. In the A = 2 \gamma\gamma chain the first nucleon's block factors out of the trace (Hecke Markov-trace functional), so the bond from nucleon 0 into nucleon 1 acts on a four-strand tail: the receiving block's word on \sigma_1, \sigma_2, followed by V^3_0 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3. The words p and n above are the production proton and neutron blocks on that tail.

Consequence. At h = 0 both free traces equal z. Dividing the bond terms by the free traces, the relative change starts at order h^4 for a bond into a proton, with coefficient (1 - z^2)/2, and at order h^5 for a bond into a neutron, with coefficient (1 - z^2)/z. At z = 1/2 these are 3/8 and 3/2.

Algebraic reduction. Over any field of characteristic \neq 2, expanding inverse crossings via \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h reduces each four-strand tail word to a linear combination of positive words evaluated by the unique Markov-trace reducer. For any first nucleon N_0 \in H_3(q), disjoint-strand factorisation multiplies both the bonded chain and the unbonded product by \mathrm{tr}_M(N_0), yielding the stated identities on the full A = 2 words.

The h^2 step. For every Y supported on strands \geq 1, \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(Y^{\uparrow}(\sigma_0\sigma_1 - \sigma_1\sigma_0)\bigr) = 0 over any commutative ring and for every z and h. Since \sigma_1 is the shift of \sigma_0, cyclicity and the Markov factorisation at the first strand reduce the two terms to \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0 Y) and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(Y\sigma_0), which are equal. The h^2 part of V^3 - 1 is this commutator, so it never contributes to the trace of a bond, whatever the receiving word.

rem:markov-z-reconciliation:
Remark Reconciliation of the Markov parameter z. Two conventions for the Markov parameter z appear in the literature and in this paper. They arise from different normalisation choices for the trace.

Convention 1 (Jones link normalisation). Producing a link invariant from the trace requires a writhe-dependent prefactor outside the trace (Jones–Markov trace); the normalisation parameter absorbed into that prefactor is

  z_{\mathrm{J}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q - 1}{(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})^2}.

At q_0 \approx 1.110, this gives z_{\mathrm{J}} \approx 0.027. The trace itself does not satisfy a two-sided rule \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n^{\pm 1}) = c^{\pm 1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for any parameter c: the Hecke quadratic relation forces the negative stabilisation to the affine value z_{-} = z_{\mathrm{m}} - (q - q^{-1}) (see below), and requiring c\,\bigl(c - (q - q^{-1})\bigr) = 1 forces c \in \{q, -q^{-1}\}, the two degenerate one-dimensional characters.

Convention 2 (Hecke tower Markov parameter). The categorical mass formula (categorical mass as Markov trace) and all mass and binding evaluations use

  z_{\mathrm{m}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^3}{q^2+1}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^2}{[2]_q},

giving z_{\mathrm{m}} \approx 0.6127 at the proton-anchored q_0.

Relation to the half-argument loop reciprocal. Writing z_{1/2} := 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) = 1/[2]_{\sqrt q}, the writhe-prefactor scalar z_{\mathrm{J}} satisfies

  z_{\mathrm{J}}
  \;=\;
  (q - 1)\,z_{1/2}^{\,2},

whereas the Hecke Markov parameter satisfies z_{\mathrm{m}}(q) = q^2\,z_{1/2}(q^2). Convention 1 normalises the Jones polynomial as a link invariant by absorbing the writhe correction into (q-1); Convention 2 evaluates the trace directly on a single Hecke generator without a writhe prefactor, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z_{\mathrm{m}}.

The negative-crossing loop value. The stabilisation rule is one-sided. For \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n) = z_{\mathrm{m}}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x), the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - (q - q^{-1}) forces

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_n^{-1})
  \;=\;
  z_{-}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x),
  \qquad
  z_{-} \;:=\; z_{\mathrm{m}} - (q - q^{-1})
  \;=\; \frac{1}{q(q^2+1)}
  \;\approx\; 0.4036

at q_0 (Markov axioms). This is the value that Hecke normal-form reduction yields for \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^{-1}); it is neither z_{\mathrm{m}} nor z_{\mathrm{m}}^{-1}.

Block weights. For any stabilisation parameter z with z_- = z - (q - q^{-1}), the Wedderburn block weights are given in closed form by the Ocneanu product

  w_\lambda
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(p_\lambda)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{x \in \lambda}
  \frac{z\,q^{c(x)} - z_{-}\,q^{-c(x)}}{q^{h(x)} - q^{-h(x)}},

with c(x) the content and h(x) the hook length of the cell x — the Ocneanu weight formula at framing ratio a^2 = z/z_{-}, verified for every \lambda \vdash n \leq 5. The single-cell case recovers \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = (z - z_{-})/(q - q^{-1}) = 1.

Monomial framing ratio and the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_N) Ocneanu family. Using \hbar_\times = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q^2 - \hbar_\times^2 = 4, the loop pair (z_{\mathrm{m}}, z_-) at z_{\mathrm{m}} = q^3/(q^2+1) satisfies

  z_{-} \;=\; \frac{1}{q(q^2+1)} , \qquad
  z_{\mathrm{m}}\,z_{-} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}} , \qquad
  a^2 \;=\; \frac{z_{\mathrm{m}}}{z_{-}} \;=\; q^4 .

Thus the two crossing loop values multiply to the inverse square of the quantum dimension (z_{\mathrm{m}}\,z_{-} = w_{(2,1)}), and the Ocneanu framing parameter is the monomial a = q^2. When a = q^N — that is, z = q^{2N}z_- — every numerator of the Ocneanu product collapses,

  z\,q^{c} - z_{-}q^{-c} \;=\; z_{-}\bigl(q^{2N+c} - q^{-c}\bigr) \;=\; z_{-}q^{N}\bigl(q^{N+c} - q^{-(N+c)}\bigr),

so with z_{-}q^{N} = 1/[N]_q the product reduces to the hook-content formula for the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_N) quantum dimension:

  w_\lambda \;=\; \frac{\dim_q\bigl(V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{sl}_N}\bigr)}{[N]_q^{\,n}} .

Solving a = q^N for z yields the one-parameter family z_N = q^N/[N]_q, whose N = 2 member is z_2 = q^2/[2]_q = q^3/(q^2+1) = z_{\mathrm{m}} (Wenzl level r = 2). For every N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}, the framing ratio is q^{2N}, the weights are \dim_q/[N]_q^{\,n}, and w_\lambda = 0 precisely when \lambda has more than N rows: a partition with more than N rows contains a cell of content -N, whose numerator factor carries [0]_q = 0. In particular, at N = 2 one obtains w_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, w_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, and the exact \mathfrak{sl}_2 row bound w_{(1^3)} = 0.

By contrast, setting z = z_{1/2} = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) gives z_- = (q^{3/2} - q^3 - q^2 + q + 1)/\bigl(q(q+1)\bigr) and a non-monomial framing ratio a^2 whose logarithmic derivative q\,(a^2)'/a^2 = -(3s^6+s^4+s^2+3)/\bigl(2(s^6+s^4-s^3-s^2-1)\bigr) (s = \sqrt q) is non-constant, so z_{1/2} belongs to z_N for no value of N and imposes no row bound.

Notation warning. The w_\lambda of this block is the Ocneanu/Markov weight y_\lambda. It is not the w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[n]_q! of the canonical q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight, which is built from the Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length dimension rather than the hook-content one. At n = 3 the two differ already at q = 1 — (1/6, 2/3, 1/6) against (1/2, 1/4, 0).

Fed z_{\mathrm{m}} = q^3/(q^2+1), the general Ocneanu formula reproduces w_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, w_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, and w_{(1^3)} = 0, with \sum_{\lambda} (\dim V_\lambda)\, w_\lambda = 1 holding identically.
prop:categorical-neutrality-saturated-sh:
Proposition Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n. Proposition (Conjecture — categorical neutrality of saturated shells). Let \mathbf{C} be a rigid braided monoidal category satisfying the QOU substrate axioms (Frobenius–Hopf substrate) and let \Phi_n be the categorical mass endomorphism at level n (mass-endomorphism conjecture). Then for every n \in \mathfrak{M} the full-twist \Delta_n^2 acts as the identity on \Phi_n:

  \Delta_n^2 \cdot \Phi_n \;=\; \Phi_n \cdot \Delta_n^2 \;=\; \Phi_n
  \qquad\text{for all } n \in \mathfrak{M}.

Equivalently, \Phi_n \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n})^{\Delta_n^2} — the categorical mass at a saturated shell is a fixed point of the full-twist action.
rem:categorical-neutrality-saturated-she: Remark Saturation, and notation for the full-twist and mass endomorphism. A nuclear shell at nucleon count n \in \mathfrak{M} = \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} is saturated in the QOU framework: the algebraic structure of the shell admits no further crossing-energy absorption. The proposition names the categorical content of saturation directly, replacing matrix-evaluation evidence (Hoefsmit seminormal forms at k = 3, \dots, 10, blocked at k \geq 12 by combinatorial growth) with a homological / algebraic-geometry statement about a global section.
rem:phi-n-global-section: Remark \Phi_n as the global section of the categorical mass functor. In the algebraic refactor of the magic-number / shell-closure framework, the categorical mass endomorphism \Phi_n acts globally, not locally. It is not built per-vortex and combined by tensor product. Instead \Phi_n forms the global section of the categorical mass functor over the rigid braided monoidal category \mathbf{C}, in the strict sense of monoidal-category global sections: \Phi_n \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) is determined by its compatibility with the Frobenius-Hopf substrate axioms across every sub-tensor-factor of A^{\otimes n}, not by an additive combination of local pieces.
rem:categorical-neutrality-saturated-she: Remark Self-conjugate support, the dropped locality assumption, and operator-level vs character-sum reading.
sec:complex-volume-intro:
The mass endomorphism \mathcal{M} carries more information than its real trace. Over \mathbb{C}, the projection defect \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\bigr) defines a single complex observable, the complex volume \mathfrak{V}(K). Here, \Pi_{\text{free}} is the factorized projector onto unlinked constituents. One defines \mathfrak{V}(K) = E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\bigr). This acts as the QOU analogue to the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(K).

The framework's two nuclear observables serve as the two real shadows of \mathfrak{V}. Binding energy forms the real part (\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}). This is the bar-even, \cosh, strong channel representing stable binding. The \beta-decay Q-value forms the imaginary part (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}). This is the bar-odd, \sinh, weak channel representing unstable decay.

The unified reconstruction \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathfrak{V} is proved. The physical conjecture asserts that the measured binding and Q-value precisely equal these real and imaginary components under a shared normalization.
conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume:
Conjecture Complex-volume unification: binding \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} and \beta-decay \mathfrak{Q}_\beta are \operatorname{Re}/\operatorname{Im} of one \mathfrak{V}=E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}). Binding and the \beta-decay Q-value form the real and imaginary parts of a single complex fibre observable — the complexified mass-endomorphism convolution-defect

  \mathfrak{V}(K)\;=\;E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M\big((\Pi_{\text{free}} - \mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\big)
  \;\in\;\mathbb{C},
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(K) = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}(K),
  \quad
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(K) = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}(K),

the QOU analogue of the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(K) [neumann-zagier1985], computed simplicially as a sum of Rogers dilogarithms of the tetrahedron parameters [neumann-cspaper, Thm. 1].
rem:volume-function-polarization-scope:
Remark Prior art: the polarization choice in the deformed volume function away from \operatorname{Re} u = 0. Murakami's parameterized volume conjecture relates the limit of \log J_N\bigl(K; \exp((u + 2\pi\sqrt{-1})/N)\bigr)/N to the volume function V(K;u) of the SL(2;\mathbb{C}) representation whose meridian has eigenvalue ratio \exp(u), through

V(K;u) = \operatorname{Im} H(K;u) - \pi \operatorname{Re}(u) - \tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{Re}(u)\operatorname{Im} v_K(u)

[murakami2006, Conjecture 2.1 and eq. (2.3), \S 2, p. 2]. For the figure-eight knot this is a theorem of Murakami and Yokota, recorded in the same section [murakami2006, \S 2, pp. 2--3]. Murakami notes that Gukov's generalization uses a different polarization: the two agree when \operatorname{Re}(u) = 0, and differ when \operatorname{Re}(u) \neq 0 by the choice of polarization [murakami2006, \S 2, p. 3]. The two \operatorname{Re}(u) terms in the formula above, which vanish on \operatorname{Re}(u) = 0, are where such a difference can appear.

What this gives here. The conjecture reads the S channel as the Chern–Simons part of the deformed complex volume of 4_1 at a substrate deformation u(q_0), and its surviving necessary condition for a sign flip of S is that u(q_0) cross the diagonal |\operatorname{Re} u| = |\operatorname{Im} u| between the anchors. On that path \operatorname{Re} u \neq 0, which is exactly the region where the published volume functions depend on the polarization. The leading harmonic form used there, and the refutation of the three candidate families built on it, are therefore statements in one polarization.

What it does not supply. It has not been checked which polarization the corpus's deformed-volume series for 4_1 realises, nor whether the refutation of the three families survives the change of polarization. Murakami does not give the explicit relation between the two conventions; he defers it to later work [murakami2006, \S 2, p. 3]. Until that check is made, the sign-flip analysis should be read as conditional on the polarization as well as on the deformed-volume channel hypothesis.
rem:channel-rotation-askey-lit: Remark The channel rotation in the Askey scheme: same eigenfunctions rotated, different measures. The bar-even (binding, \cosh) and bar-odd (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta, \sinh) channels of the complex volume \mathfrak{V} constitute a single Askey-scheme family evaluated through a rotation. Both the rotation and its limits are classical.
conj:whipple-rotation-intertwining: Conjecture Whipple–rotation intertwining: the channel rotation acts on the toroidal family as the degree–order (winding) exchange. The archimedean shadow of the fibre-level channel rotation (x, q) \mapsto (ix, q^{-1}) acts on the toroidal channel family P^{\mu}_{\nu - 1/2}(\cosh\eta)\, e^{i\mu\theta} e^{i\nu\varphi} as the Whipple degree–order exchange: it swaps the two winding gradings (\mu, \nu) \mapsto (\nu, \mu) and is involutive on the ladder data.
rem:complex-volume-character-variety-pat: Remark Bound \leftrightarrow free as a character-variety path: the deformation reading of \mathfrak{V}. The interpolation between the bound and free projections of Complex-volume unification constitutes a path. The bar-odd channel provides its holonomy. No structure beyond the deformation itself is required to rotate between the bound and free states.
prop:color-spacetime-s5-factorization:
Proposition Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5. Let K be a Bring-embeddable knot evaluated through the categorical Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on the Hecke algebra H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q), whose 2+3=5 irreducible representations constitute the Bring fivefold, with Bring's five homogeneous coordinates split as spacetime (x_0, x_1) and color (x_2, x_3, x_4). The substrate Galois group S_5 contains the block-diagonal product

  S_2 \times S_3 \hookrightarrow S_5.

Then:

  1. The factorization S_2 \times S_3 \hookrightarrow S_5 acts faithfully.
  2. The color factor S_3 fixes every spacetime coordinate. The spacetime factor S_2 fixes every color coordinate. The two sectors remain orthogonal.
  3. Every additive homomorphism from the connected phase parameter \mathbb{R} to a finite group is trivial.
rem:mass-modulus-em-phase-color-grading: Remark Mass is the modulus, electromagnetism the phase, color the S_3 grading of one trace. The factorization of Color and spacetime are orthogonal S_2\times S_3 factors of the Bring Galois group S_5 fixes how the three observables of a Bring-embeddable knot sit on the single trace scalar \mathrm{tr}_M and its trace algebra H_2(q)\oplus H_3(q).

prose:intro-hecke-chi-closed-forms: The Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) carries two complementary coordinate charts: the Markov u-coordinate adapted to recursive braid-word reduction, and the Wedderburn character coordinate \chi^\lambda indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n. This section derives the explicit change of basis between the u-coordinate discharge rules and the irreducible Hecke characters \chi^\lambda, and initiates the closed-form evaluation of \chi^\lambda beginning with the totally symmetric three-strand representation V_{(3)}.
rem:u-coordinate-discharges:

rem:hecke-algebra-type-scaffold:
Remark Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(R, q): the Lean type and its defining relations. The Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is the unital associative algebra with generators \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{n-2} modulo three defining relations: the quadratic relation (R1), the far-commutation relation (R2), and the braid cubic relation (R3). Its full type-theoretic realization decomposes into four constructions: a free R-module on B_n, a multiplication structure, the quotient by the three relations, and the per-block Wedderburn decomposition (the q-deformed Schur–Weyl splitting \sum_\lambda y_\lambda = 1).

Here the abstract generators, formal signed words, defining relations and Plancherel completeness are taken as hypotheses, and results downstream assume the defining relations and the Wedderburn decomposition. These hypotheses are to be discharged for each n by the relation quotient and the Murphy seminormal form, which are not constructed here.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:markov-trace-operator-construction:
Remark Markov-trace operator construction. The Jones–Wenzl Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M : \mathbf{B}_\infty \to \mathbb{R} on the inductive limit of braid groups is uniquely characterised by the M1–M4 axioms (Jones 1985 / Wenzl 1988). One realises it as a single operator on the von Neumann inductive-limit hyperfinite \mathrm{II}_1 factor in five stages: a per-n Hilbert representation, an inductive embedding \iota_n : V_n \hookrightarrow V_{n+1}, the inductive limit V_\infty = \varinjlim V_n, the trace state on \bigcup_n H_n, and the bicommutant closure \mathcal{M} := (\bigcup_n H_n)''. On \mathcal{M}, the trace \mathrm{tr}_M provides the unique faithful normal trace up to scaling.

The per-n representation, the inductive embedding, and the GNS bicommutant factor hosting \mathrm{tr}_M are taken as hypotheses by the results downstream. The operator-algebra steps—the GNS state and the bicommutant closure—are what supply them for each n.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Generic categorical q-deformation identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; one specialises only their archimedean realisation here.
rem:chi-v3-closed-form-proof:
Remark Formal proof of the V_{(3)} per-irrep character difference closed form: \chi_{(3)}(\beta_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\beta_p) = -(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)/(4q) = -(q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1})/4, with explicit \varepsilon^k pattern via polynomial + geometric decomposition.   \boxed{
    \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
    \;=\; -\frac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q}
    \;=\; -\frac{q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1}}{4}
  }

conj:qbeta-c-k-closed-forms:
Conjecture Closed-form conjectures for c_4, c_5, c_6, c_7 in the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder (z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) frame). Closed-form conjectures for the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder coefficients c_4, c_5, c_6, c_7.

In terms of the Hopf–Jones seed c_3 = -2 and the Kashiwara coupling b, the conjectured closed forms are

  c_4 = c_3\, b^4 = -2 b^4, \qquad
  c_5 = -\bigl(b^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\bigr), \qquad
  c_6 = c_3^2\, b^2 = 4 b^2, \qquad
  c_7 = c_3^3 = -8.

Scope. The ladder these coefficients belong to is formulated at the auxiliary loop parameter z_{\mathrm{aux}} = \sqrt q/(q+1); at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), no corresponding c_k ladder has been derived. The conjecture therefore applies to the z_{\mathrm{aux}} = \sqrt q/(q+1) expansion only.

The comparison of these forms with extracted values, the open derivation paths, and the precision record are in Open derivation paths, precision leverage, and SDP evidence for the c_k.

rem:chi-v111-via-sign-substitution:
Remark V_{(1,1,1)} per-irrep character difference via sign-representation substitution \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1}. V_(1,1,1) per-irrep character via sign-rep substitution.

V_{(1,1,1)} constitutes the antisymmetric 1-d irrep of H_3(q). The character is derived directly via scalar arithmetic (analogous to V_{(3)}) using the sign-rep action:

  • \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1}
  • \sigma_i^{-1} \mapsto -q
  • averaged \mapsto -(q + q^{-1})/2

Applied to the canonical typed-\mathbf{B}_3 braids:

  • \mathcal{B}_p (uud): 6\sigma + 3\sigma^{-1} + 2 averaged
  • \mathcal{B}_n (udd): 5\sigma + 4\sigma^{-1} + 2 averaged

yields:

  • \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) = (-q^{-1})^6 \cdot (-q)^3 \cdot (-(q+q^{-1})/2)^2 = -q^{-3} \cdot (q+q^{-1})^2/4
  • \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) = (-q^{-1})^5 \cdot (-q)^4 \cdot (-(q+q^{-1})/2)^2 = -q^{-1} \cdot (q+q^{-1})^2/4

Difference (proved):

  \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   = -\frac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q^5}.
rem:chi-v21-hoefsmit-matrix-derivation:
Remark V_{(2,1)} Hoefsmit 2\times 2 matrix derivation: scalar trace + Hecke-quadratic identities + Laurent decomposition of the closed form -(q^4+1)(q^2-1)/(4q^3). V_(2,1) Hoefsmit 2\times2 matrix derivation — partial closure.

V_{(2,1)} provides the 2-dimensional Hoefsmit irrep of H_3(q). Unlike V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} (1-d, scalar arithmetic), V_{(2,1)} requires the full 2\times2 matrix representation:

  \sigma_0 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} q & 0 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  \sigma_1 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} d_1 & b \\ b & d_2 \end{pmatrix}

with d_1 = -q^{-1}/(q^2+1), d_2 = q^3/(q^2+1), b^2 = d_1 d_2 + 1.

Uniqueness of the diagonal assignment (d_1, d_2). With \sigma_0 = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) fixed as above, the braid relation \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 \sigma_1 admits the unique diagonal assignment (d_1, d_2) shown (up to the sign of b, and the degenerate b = 0). The transposed pair (d_2, d_1) satisfies the Hecke quadratic relation, has the same trace q - q^{-1} and determinant -1, and yields the same b^2 — all four of those quantities are symmetric in d_1, d_2 — yet fails the braid relation and therefore does not define a representation of B_3. At q = 1 the representation reduces to the classical Young orthogonal matrix s_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -1/2 & \sqrt3/2 \\ \sqrt3/2 & 1/2 \end{pmatrix} on the two-dimensional irreducible representation of S_3.

  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   = -\frac{(q^4 + 1)(q^2 - 1)}{4 q^3}.

prop:categorical-chain-convergence-mecha:
Proposition Convergence of \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{cat}}'s infinite product: per-knot c(K) brane-tower bound + inter-knot linking-number locality (Habiro-ring interpretation). Conditional on exponential decay of the archimedean brane-tower truncation remainder. Categorical-chain convergence: per-knot finite truncation + inter-knot linking-number locality.

The categorical-derivation precision ladder \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{cat}} is formally an infinite product in the Habiro ring (cyclotomic-Pochhammer completion of \mathbb{Z}[q]). For any single isolated knot, this product reduces to a finite truncation at sub-CODATA precision through two convergence mechanisms.
rem:categorical-chain-convergence-mechan:
Remark Truncation depth needed for free-neutron \beta-decay at 1 ppb. This remark records the truncation depth that Mechanism 1 gives for free-neutron \beta-decay at the substrate value q_0.

For free-neutron \beta-decay, truncation at N = 3 suffices for 1 ppb precision. Physical predictions rely on this finite truncation, not the formal infinite product.
